summary: Sable Health is evaluating Redwood Private for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment to serve internal clinician-assist models. Primary concerns: offline update process, hardware/PCIe/NVLink constraints, KMS/HSM for keys, audit logs and retention, model acceptance testing, and timeline for a pilot in Q4. Redwood AE + SE walked through deployment modes, offline update workflows, and potential BOMs for A100 vs H100. Next steps: send security artifacts, pilot BOM, schedule workshop.

Latency vs cost tradeoffs, quantization and batching
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Maya our SE. How are you all?
[00:07] Elena: Hi Jordan, thanks, yes, good. I'm Elena, Head of AI at Sable Health. Marcus and Priya are with me.
[00:11] Marcus: Hey.
[00:12] Priya: Hi.
[00:14] Maya: Great, quick agenda, we'll do a discovery to understand your constraints, then we can talk through on-prem air-gap options, offline updates, and sizing. Sound good?
[00:21] Elena: Yep that's perfect. We're a hospital system, so this is regulated - PHI flows, so we need everything air-gapped and auditable. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs on-prem but leaning on-prem for now.
[00:33] Jordan: Totally, makes sense. Can you walk me through current infra? Marcus, maybe you?
[00:37] Marcus: Sure. We run a private datacenter, are not connected to internet for clinical workloads. We have a procurement list, approved vendors only. Currently NVMe storage backend, Mellanox switches, and a couple of racks with 8x A100 40GB each for training. For inference we want something smaller footprint but with low latency for clinician workflows - sub 200 ms target per request ideally.
[01:00] Maya: When you say sub 200 ms, is that end-to-end from clinician UI or pure token latency?
[01:05] Elena: From UI - so total call plus any pre/post processing. Most calls will be short prompts, 200-400 tokens.
[01:12] Jordan: Got it. Two threads we need to align on: security/process and hardware. On security, Priya, what are the must-haves?
[01:19] Priya: SOC2 is table stakes. We also need audit logs retained for seven years, SSO with SAML integration, RBAC for model access, and hardware KMS integration ideally with our HSM. No egress allowed from the air-gapped network; updates have to be done via signed offline packages.
[01:33] Maya: Okay offline updates and signed packages are something Redwood Private supports via our offline installer and signed model bundles. We have a documented process: we provide a signed tar bundle and a verifier tool that runs inside the customer's air-gapped environment. It's similar to on-prem packages we've done with other health customers.
[01:48] Marcus: What's the verifier? Does it call home?
[01:50] Maya: No, it runs locally. It checks the bundle signature against a public key that you provision. We can work with your KMS/HSM workflow to store the public keys locally. The private signing happens in Redwood's control plane in our secure environment, but the bundle contains a signature - you don't need outbound connectivity to validate.
[02:05] Priya: That sounds promising, but we need to review the exact crypto algorithms and whether that mesh's our HSM. Also we need to ensure reproducible checksums and an audit trail that ties to our logging.
[02:15] Jordan: We'll send the crypto spec and the signed-bundle workflow from our security pack.
[02:20] Elena: Good. Hardware - Marcus, you mentioned A100s. We may consider H100s for new procurement but procurement cycles are long. Would Redwood support H100-based inference? And what's the difference for throughput/latency?
[02:31] Maya: Yes, H100 is supported in our runtime; generally gives a 1.5-2x throughput improvement on certain models especially FP16/TF32 paths. For quantized 4-bit models the gap can be smaller. NVLink topology matters for multi-GPU KV cache sharing if you want shard-based serving across GPUs.
[02:46] Marcus: We don't have NVLink across racks; NVLink is only within the nodes we procured previously. For inference we prefer single node small clusters. We need to know if Redwood can do single-GPU inference well with our model sizes.
[02:57] Maya: Absolutely - our runtime supports single-GPU and multi-GPU. For large context models, you might hit memory limits and we'd suggest model quantization or offloading. We also do continuous batching and prefix KV caching, which helps with throughput while keeping tail latency controlled.
[03:13] Elena: Quick question on model artifacts: Are the model weights stored encrypted at rest on the nodes and how does key rotation work?
[03:19] Jordan: We support encrypted-at-rest images and integration with customer KMS/HSM for key unwrap. Key rotation is supported but in air-gapped environments we recommend a maintenance window where new keys are provisioned and bundles re-signed.
[03:31] Priya: Do you have an architecture diagram of a fully private deployment?
[03:34] Jordan: Yes, we'll send the private deployment diagram and the network checklist. It shows the control plane optionality: full offline where you host the control plane, or hybrid where control plane is in our private VPC and only signed bundles come in. For regulated workloads you usually go full private control plane.
[03:50] Marcus: Full private control plane means we'll host Redwood's control plane components behind our firewall?
[03:54] Maya: Correct. Either we ship a private control plane appliance you run inside the network or we provide the on-prem package to install with your orchestration. No outbound egress needed after initial key exchange and bundle import.
[04:07] Elena: Performance testing - we want to do an internal benchmark with our prompts and dataset. How does the pilot work?
[04:12] Jordan: Typical is a two-week pilot: we ship a pilot BOM with recommended GPU topology, you stand up the environment, we help provision the bundle, run a benchmark harness with your test prompts, and measure latency/throughput and cost. After that we do a tuning pass - batching, quantization profiles, runtime kernel selection.
[04:28] Marcus: Are there any compatibility restrictions on the OS or scheduler? We run RHEL and Slurm for cluster management.
[04:34] Maya: We support RHEL/CentOS-compatible kernels. For job scheduling we can integrate with Slurm or run as a service behind an HTTP gateway. For air-gapped installs we typically provide a container runtime and systemd service.
[04:45] Priya: Back to audit retention - you said the control plane kept logs. If we host the control plane, do logs stay local?
[04:51] Jordan: Yes - if you host the private control plane all audit logs never leave your environment. Our console tooling can be run locally, and we provide log exporters to your SIEM.
[05:00] Elena: What about fallback? If a model update fails, can the system automatically rollback to last-known-good? We can't have clinicians blocked.
[05:06] Maya: We support canary rollouts and automatic rollback policies. Bundle deployment can be staged to a canary node, health checks are run, and if the canary fails we stop the rollout. Those policies are configurable and we can tie them to your acceptance tests.
[05:20] Marcus: Any special network ports? Again we plan to lock down everything.
[05:24] Jordan: We'll include a minimal network checklist - ports for internal control plane components, no outbound ports required unless you opt for hybrid control plane during onboarding.
[05:33] Elena: Pricing - high level, what should we expect for a private license vs hosted?
[05:37] Jordan: High-level - hosted is usage-based per token; dedicated reserved capacity is monthly commit for predictable throughput; private on-prem is a platform license plus support and optional enterprise features. We'll send a ballpark pricing deck.
[05:49] Priya: For procurement we need a draft contract and list of supported third-party vendors.
[05:53] Jordan: We'll attach an NDA and procurement checklist.
[05:57] Elena: Two technical nitpicks - offline updates need to be reproducible (we want deterministic checksums), and we need a path to rollback model weights quickly.
[06:05] Maya: Deterministic checksums are part of the signed bundle. Rollback is handled via image snapshots in the storage layer and via our bundle versioning; you can pin versions and we keep previous versions in the local registry.
[06:18] Marcus: For GPUs, if we go with A100 80GB or H100 80GB, what's the recommended memory/perf tradeoff if we want to serve a 13B model at 2-4 concurrent requests?
[06:28] Maya: 13B quantized to Q4 will easily fit on 40GB A100 for single-GPU with good latency; for higher concurrency H100 gives better throughput. If you want multi-shard or longer contexts (4k+), consider 80GB class GPUs or offloading. We'll give sizing recommendations in the BOM.
[06:45] Elena: Great. Any blockers from Redwood side for using our HSM?
[06:49] Maya: We can integrate with PKCS#11 compatible HSMs. We'll need connection details and to validate the key wrap/unwrap flow. In air-gapped environments the HSM keys never leave the network; we just call into the HSM locally.
[07:02] Jordan: Alright, sounds like we have clear next steps. Marcus and Priya will provide environment constraints and vendor approvals; we'll send security docs and the BOM, and schedule an on-site or virtual workshop.
[07:13] Elena: Sounds good. Quick question from me - what about model updates frequency? We typically update models every 4-6 weeks after validation.
[07:20] Maya: That's common. For air-gapped updates we'd create signed bundles per release and you can choose weekly or monthly cadence. We recommend canarying major updates.
[07:29] Marcus: One more thing - do you support GPU topology where some nodes are inference-only and others do training? We want separation.
[07:35] Maya: Yes you can separate training and inference clusters. The private control plane can schedule to specific nodes based on labels.
[07:42] Jordan: Ok folks, we'll recap after the call and list the artifacts we'll send. Anything else?
[07:47] Elena: No, that's it. Thanks.
[07:49] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the security pack and a proposed BOM.
[07:53] [crosstalk / audio blip]
[07:55] Jordan: Action items as discussed. Talk soon.
